title: Saurfang's Rebellion
summary: The Fourth War divides the Horde as Saurfang's dissent, Baine's rescue, and rival loyalist paths converge on Orgrimmar.
opening: The Horde's war reopened an argument about what it was becoming. Saurfang's refusal gave that argument a face, but not every Horde champion chose his side.
reviewNote: Preserve the differences between the Saurfang and Sylvanas loyalist branches while reviewing the final campaign scenes. Editorial chapter research tasks retained here: Establish the war's political and moral split. Trace the choices that made his opposition visible. Follow the rescue and the cooperation it required. Compare the branch perspectives on the campaign's end.

chapters.title: The Horde fractures
chapters.body: The Fourth War divided the Horde over the meaning of its own actions. Duty and obedience no longer offered the same answer to every champion.

chapters.title: Saurfang's refusal
chapters.body: Saurfang’s refusal gave that division a face. His choices made opposition visible within a people already at war.

chapters.title: The rescue of Baine
chapters.body: Baine’s rescue brought unlikely cooperation into the struggle. The Horde’s future had become a question fought within its own allegiances.

chapters.title: Before Orgrimmar
chapters.body: At Orgrimmar, rebellion and loyalty approached a reckoning from different sides. Their separate perspectives remain part of the unfinished telling.
